questions.q: Which MongoDB edition is required to use the built-in audit log?
options: MongoDB Enterprise or Atlas — auditing is not available in Community Server
Community Server, with no additional configuration needed
Auditing is available identically across all editions
Auditing requires a separate third-party product entirely
questions.explain: Like encryption at rest, MongoDB's audit log is an Enterprise/Atlas feature, not part of Community Server.

questions.q: What risk does binding mongod to 0.0.0.0 create?
options: The instance becomes reachable from any network that can route to the host, not just trusted application servers
It disables authentication automatically
It prevents the database from accepting any connections at all
It only affects the legacy HTTP interface, nothing else
questions.explain: 0.0.0.0 means mongod listens on every network interface, widening the reachable attack surface far beyond what's needed.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend instead of binding to 0.0.0.0?
options: Bind to specific, known-trusted addresses via net.bindIp
Disable networking entirely and only allow local connections forever
Leave bindIp unset so MongoDB picks automatically
Bind only to IPv6 addresses, never IPv4
questions.explain: net.bindIp should list specific trusted addresses so the database is reachable only by the application tier that needs it.

questions.q: What is the legacy HTTP interface, and what's the recommended stance on it?
options: An old status interface on the database port range, disabled by default since MongoDB 3.2, but worth explicitly verifying is off
A required interface for all MongoDB replication traffic
A modern Atlas-only feature that should always be enabled
An interface that was never a security concern
questions.explain: The legacy HTTP interface was a real historical attack surface; it's off by default now but config drift can re-enable it, so it's worth confirming explicitly.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an audit log, as distinguished from authentication and RBAC in this lesson?
options: It's an after-the-fact record of who did what and when, for compliance and investigation — not a preventive control
It actively blocks unauthorized actions before they happen
It replaces the need for authentication entirely
It only logs successful queries, never authentication events
questions.explain: The audit log is compared to SQL Server Audit — a historical record for compliance and investigation, distinct from the preventive controls of auth and RBAC.
